슈퍼마켓.x: I bought milk at the supermarket near my house.
슈퍼마켓.e: From English 'supermarket'; usually shortened to 슈퍼, often a small neighborhood store.

당근.ex: 저는 어렸을 때 당근을 정말 싫어했어요.
당근.x: I really hated carrots when I was little.
당근.e: In casual speech 당근이지! is slang for 'of course!', a pun on 당연하지.

칭찬하다.ex: 부장님이 회의에서 제 보고서를 많이 칭찬했어요.
칭찬하다.x: My manager praised my report a lot in the meeting.

잡다.m: to catch, to grab, to hold; to take (a taxi)
잡다.ex: 길을 건널 때는 아이의 손을 꼭 잡으세요.
잡다.x: Hold your child's hand tightly when crossing the street.
잡다.t: Regular verb (잡아요); also 택시를 잡다 'hail a taxi' and 약속을 잡다 'set an appointment'.

멍.x: I fell and got a bruise on my leg.
멍.t: The verb is 들다: 멍이 들다, 'to get a bruise.'

창고.ex: 안 쓰는 물건은 창고에 넣어 두었어요.
창고.x: I put the things I don't use in the storage room.

낡다.m: to be old, worn out, shabby (of things)
낡다.ex: 이 아파트는 오래돼서 시설이 많이 낡았어요.
낡다.x: This apartment is old, so the facilities are really worn out.
낡다.e: Used only for things; for people getting old, use 늙다.
낡다.t: Usually used in the past form to describe a state: 옷이 낡았어요 'The clothes are worn out.'

증가.ex: 올해는 관광객 수의 증가가 눈에 띄어요.
증가.x: This year the rise in the number of tourists is noticeable.

창피하다.x: I was so embarrassed because I fell in front of people.
창피하다.e: Sino-Korean, but the syllables don't help here; learn it as a whole.
창피하다.t: 창피하다 is public embarrassment; 부끄럽다 can also mean shy or ashamed of yourself.

중단하다.m: to stop, to halt, to suspend
중단하다.x: It rained a lot, so they stopped the game.

봉사.x: I did volunteer work at a nursing home during the break.
봉사.t: The usual collocation is 봉사 활동을 하다, 'to do volunteer activities.'

정수기.ex: 사무실에 정수기가 있어서 물을 사지 않아요.
정수기.x: There's a water purifier in the office, so I don't buy water.
정수기.t: Many Korean homes rent a 정수기 monthly, with regular filter service included.

참을성.e: 참을, the modifier of 참다 'to endure', + 성 'quality': the quality of enduring.

위선적.x: That politician's behavior is so hypocritical.
위선적.e: -적 = '-ic, -al,' turning nouns into descriptive words: 위선적, 가식적, 이타적.
위선적.t: -적 words describe nouns with 인: 위선적인 사람 (a hypocritical person).

장모.ex: 장모님이 해 주신 김치가 정말 맛있어요.
장모.x: The kimchi my mother-in-law made is really delicious.
장모.t: Say 장모님 when speaking to her or about her politely.

복수.x: She resolved to take revenge for her family.
복수.t: Homonym: 복수 (複數) also means 'plural'. A revenge drama is called a 복수극.

재구성하다.m: to reconstruct, to reorganize, to rearrange
재구성하다.x: Police reconstructed the incident from witness statements.

왕세자.ex: 왕세자는 어릴 때부터 왕이 되기 위한 교육을 받았어요.
왕세자.x: The crown prince was educated from childhood to become king.

학제.x: Korea's school system is six years of elementary, three of middle, and three of high school.
학제.t: In 학제 간 연구 'interdisciplinary research', 학제 is a homonym meaning 'between fields'.

법인.ex: 사업이 커지자 그는 회사를 법인으로 전환했습니다.
법인.x: As the business grew, he turned the company into a corporation.
법인.e: Literally 'legal person' — a company the law treats like a person.
법인.t: Pronounced [버빈]; 법인 카드 means a corporate credit card.

옵션.ex: 옵션 거래는 위험이 커서 주의해야 해요.
옵션.x: Options trading is very risky, so you have to be careful.
옵션.e: From English 'option'; in apartment ads, 풀옵션 means fully furnished with appliances.

목회자.ex: 그 목회자는 지역 사회를 위해 봉사 활동을 많이 해요.
목회자.x: That pastor does a lot of volunteer work for the local community.
목회자.e: Literally 'one who shepherds the congregation'; -자 = person: 과학자, 운전자.
목회자.t: 목사 is the title (목사님); 목회자 is the broader, more formal word for clergy.

호젓하다.ex: 우리는 호젓한 산길을 따라 천천히 걸었어요.
호젓하다.x: We walked slowly along a quiet, secluded mountain path.
호젓하다.e: Describes a peaceful, out-of-the-way spot, or being pleasantly alone there.
호젓하다.t: Pronounced [호저타다]: the ㅅ batchim sounds like ㄷ and merges with ㅎ into ㅌ.

퇴폐적.ex: 그 영화는 퇴폐적인 분위기 때문에 비판을 받았어요.
퇴폐적.x: That movie was criticized for its decadent atmosphere.
퇴폐적.t: Pronounced [퇴페적]; before nouns, everyday speech prefers 퇴폐적인.
